questions.q: Total number of regions in which ' $n$ ' coplanar lines can divide the plane, it is known that no two lines are parallel and no three of them are concurrent, is equal to
questions.solution:
Let number of regions for $n$ lines be $R(n)$. Clearly, $R(1)=2, R(2)=4, \ldotsR(n)=R(n-1)+n \text{ i.e. } R(n)-R(n-1)=n$
Putting $n=2,3, \ldots, n$ and then adding, we get
$R(n)-R(1)=2+3+\ldots+n\begin{aligned} & =2+2+3+4+\ldots+n=1+\frac{n(n+1)}{2} \\ & =\frac{n^2+n+2}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $According to Newton-Raphson method, the value of \sqrt{12}$ upto three places of decimal will be
questions.solution:
Let $x=\sqrt{12}\Rightarrow \quad x^2=12\Rightarrow \quad x^2-12=0$
Let $\quad f(x)=x^2-12$
The first approximation in the Newton-Raphson method is given by
$x_1=x_0-\frac{f\left(x_0\right)}{f^{\prime}\left(x_0\right)}=x_0-\frac{x_0^2-12}{2 x_0}=\frac{x_0^2+12}{2 x_0}\because \quad 3 < \sqrt{12} < 3.5$
We can take $x_0=3.5\therefore \quad x_1=\frac{(3.5)^2+12}{2 \times 3.5}=\frac{12.25+12}{7}=\frac{24.25}{7}=3.464$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
$a, b, c$ are prime numbers, $x$ is an even number, $y$ is an odd number. Which of the following is/are never true?
I. $a+x=b$
II. $b+y=c$
III. $a b=c$
IV. $a+b=c$
questions.solution: Since, c is a prime number so it can have only two factors 1 and c. $a b=c$ gives two more factors of $c$ as a and b , which is not possible.
